subject: Ops observability follow-up — agreed test matrix & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finops.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, Apr 05, 2026 at 16:12 PDT
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed test matrix (observability & ops)

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from my side and a proposed set of tests so we can objectively compare Redwood vs the hyperscaler path you mentioned:

Summary of differentiators we covered:
- Unified runtime with built-in KV/prefix caching and automatic batching (helps tail latency).
- Per-request telemetry and token-level cost accounting exposed via the Console API.
- Tracing hooks and automatic span linkage for OpenTelemetry / Datadog.
- Deployment options: Hosted API, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC) for network isolation.

Proposed test matrix (please confirm priority and timeline):
1) Latency & tail tests — p50/p95/p99 for 1/4/8 token responses and for 128/512 token responses (measure both with and without prefix caching).
2) End-to-end trace continuity — ensure single request creates linked spans from API gateway → Redwood runtime → model exec; verify in Datadog/Grafana.
3) Cost telemetry — per-token and per-request cost breakdown for real payloads, including batching effects.
4) Streaming & function-calling — validate partial streaming, content length headers, and structured JSON outputs for downstream services.
5) Observability surface — dashboards, logs, and retention (audit logs for SOC2).

Attachments / links: demo recording and a skeleton test plan (I asked Prioym to flesh out the runbook).

Next steps: please confirm which tests you want prioritized and any sample payloads or traffic patterns we should use. If ok, propose a 2-week window starting Apr 6 for an initial baseline run.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-demo-20260405.mp4 (video/mp4)]
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@finops.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, Apr 05, 2026 at 18:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed test matrix (observability & ops)

Appreciate the clear recap — that matches our notes. Prioritization from our side:
1) End-to-end p95/p99 latency (important for SLAs)
2) Trace continuity into Datadog — we need span linkage to our request IDs
3) Cost telemetry and per-token visibility (finance will audit this)
4) Streaming/structured outputs as a blocker for our ingestion pipeline

We can provide sample payloads and a small synthetic workload for the baseline. SOC2/security will want to see audit retention and where logs live — adding Jenna Park (security) to loop her in.

2-week window works for a baseline run. Can you confirm whether you need a VPC/private deployment or if hosted is fine for initial tests? Also please share the runbook and any curl examples we can run from our side.

—Samira
Head of Platform Engineering, FinOps AI
From: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finops.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Apr 06, 2026 at 09:40 PDT
Subject: Redwood ops test plan & curl examples

Hi Samira — thanks, looping in the SE runbook. I've attached a short test-plan PDF and a shell script with curl examples you can run from your environment. High level approach below and exact steps are in the doc:

Test plan highlights:
- Baseline: 500 sequential requests + 1000 concurrent small-batch requests (batch sizes 1,4,8).
- Long-response test: 200 requests with 512-token outputs; measure memory/KV cache hit rates.
- Trace test: inject header "x-redwood-trace-id" with your request id; we'll verify span linkage in Datadog.
- Streaming test: open SSE/HTTP2 stream and validate chunking + partial JSON assemble behavior.
- Cost run: run 10k tokens-worth across a mix of payloads and capture per-token accounting.

Observability data we'll capture (and how to retrieve it):
- Per-request spans (OTLP) and example traces accessible in Datadog — sample query provided in doc.
- Per-route token and cost metrics surfaced via Console API and exported to your billing export (CSV).
- Pre-built Grafana dashboard with p50/p95/p99, queue depth, batch-size distribution.

Attachments: redwood-test-plan-ops.pdf, curl-examples.sh

If you can drop the sample payloads into the shared doc (link below) I can schedule a canary run in our staging region on Apr 07.
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBC-test-plan

—Prioym
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
